svg.title: What calls what across the FerroHEALTH family
svg.desc: Five products reach each other only over published protocols. FerroEHR, the openEHR CDR, is reached over the openEHR ITS-REST API and AQL, which any application can call directly, and it validates coded values against FerroTERM, the FHIR terminology server, as a client. FerroBRIDGE reads FerroEHR over ITS-REST, calls FerroTERM to look up and translate codes, exchanges resources with HL7 FHIR over its FHIR face in both directions, receives clinical HL7 Version 2 messages over MLLP, and writes typed rows into an OMOP Common Data Model database over SQL. FerroFORMS, the form builder, is paused and drawn in grey: a clinician uses it in a browser, and it expands value sets against FerroTERM and commits compositions to FerroEHR over ITS-REST. Three services frame the data path: FerroPIX, the Master Patient Index, owns identity and the IHE profiles, and FerroEHR is to look the subject of each EHR up there as a client over PIXm and PDQm; applications send FerroFED, the federation gateway, an ordinary AQL query, and it asks FerroPIX where the record is, then dispatches the query to FerroEHR and to other organisations' openEHR CDRs as federation nodes; and FerroTASK, the planned task planning and decision support server, drawn dashed, reads FerroEHR over ITS-REST and AQL and commits the state of each plan back to it. Each server checks the access tokens it is handed against the deployment's own authorization server, so no FerroHEALTH service holds the key every server depends on. A frame around the seven marks one FerroHEALTH instance serving one tenant; clinicians, applications, FHIR, HL7 Version 2 senders, OMOP and other organisations sit outside it. Under the frame, a band holds the four shared libraries the products are built from, which never run on their own: FerroAUTH authenticates callers and makes the policy decision, issuing no token, FerroAUDIT writes the audit trail and the EHDS access record, FerroUI holds the components of the operator consoles, every one of them reactive, and FerroSYS holds the system plumbing every product shares, from secrets and configuration to telemetry, health, the HTTP stack and the usage report.

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: SHARED LIBRARIES · BUILT INTO THE PRODUCTS, NEVER RUN ON THEIR OWN
SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD-10, ICD-11, RxNorm, UCUM · the FHIR terminology API
A dashed outline is a server not running yet, and a dashed line a call into one.
